decision_required: Evaluator calibration sample and tolerated errors

criteria.name: Baseline identity and official scope
criteria.definition: The current student plan, competition year, division and linked syllabus version must be explicit and content-bound.
criteria.measurement: Read actual bytes; compare SHA256; enumerate ten week rows and all 60 syllabus rows; compare official theory/practical flags.
criteria.pass: Pinned bytes and all expected IDs/flags agree.
criteria.fail: Hash, year, division, topic or flag mismatch.
criteria.uncertainty: Unavailable baseline or unresolved version conflict remains uncertain.

examples.normal: Earlier 240-minute HTML cannot replace the current 120-minute baseline.
examples.fault_or_boundary: Changing the file while keeping an old digest fails.

criteria.expected_effect: Detect silent baseline or scope substitution.
criteria.limits: A pinned copy does not prove the live official page stayed unchanged.
criteria.implementation: See tools/quality.py and the implementation table in quality-specification.md; semantic judgments remain reviewed records.

criteria.name: Planned coverage and achieved depth
criteria.definition: Scheduled exposure, explanation, guided application and independent transfer are different claims.
criteria.object: Every official topic and each selected objective
criteria.measurement: Record official modes, placement, required components, evidence and help level separately. A full-syllabus completion claim needs evidence for every required mode/component.
criteria.pass: All selected obligations have matching evidence at the claimed depth; no omitted official obligations in a full claim.
criteria.fail: A practical requirement is claimed complete using only a concept description, cached output, or a different named model.
criteria.uncertainty: Scheduled but unperformed work is not_run, not failure of a student.

examples.normal: Running Random Forest does not establish that Bagging and Gradient Boosting were run.
examples.fault_or_boundary: A theory-only topic does not acquire a practical obligation just because code is available.

criteria.expected_effect: Expose gaps without turning a topic mention into mastery.
criteria.limits: Official grouping and the plan's expanded obligations must be distinguished; a course completion is not exam success.
criteria.implementation: See tools/quality.py and the implementation table in quality-specification.md; semantic judgments remain reviewed records.

criteria.name: Time and workload accounting
criteria.definition: Class time includes all activities performed during the class; required and optional outside work are separate.
criteria.measurement: Sum theory, noncoding and coding blocks; count written practice inside noncoding; list setup, support, execution, feedback and retry time without double counting.
criteria.pass: Every class totals 120 minutes and current plan allocations are preserved; required outside work is disclosed separately.
criteria.fail: A class totals 240 minutes, adds written practice on top of 120, or relabels required syllabus work as optional.
criteria.uncertainty: Arithmetic can pass while actual completion time remains unobserved; workload acceptability awaits a user decision.

examples.normal: Week 1 is 20 + 20 + 80; its written practice is inside the 20.
examples.fault_or_boundary: A six-hour mock exam cannot be counted inside a two-hour class.

criteria.limits: An estimate cannot establish feasibility; no universal acceptable homework limit is inferred.
criteria.implementation: See tools/quality.py and the implementation table in quality-specification.md; semantic judgments remain reviewed records.

criteria.name: Prerequisite diagnosis and support
criteria.definition: Readiness is demonstrated prerequisite behavior or an explicit support route before its first use, not an age label.
criteria.object: Python and mathematical prerequisites of each objective
criteria.measurement: Record a concrete task, expected behavior, actual response, help used, diagnosis and support placement. Diagnose variables/control flow, functions/return, lists/indexing, files/errors; ratios before metrics and axes before reduction.
criteria.pass: Every dependency is demonstrated under stated help or bridged by a scheduled support activity before use, according to the agreed readiness policy.
criteria.fail: The material depends on an unintroduced or diagnosed-missing skill with no prior support.
criteria.uncertainty: No learner response means unknown readiness. Cutoffs such as 4/5 in the HTML are proposals until their use is agreed and calibrated.

examples.normal: Printing a value does not demonstrate returning it from a function.
examples.fault_or_boundary: A student who needs help is routed to support rather than silently labeled ready.

criteria.limits: This diagnoses named tasks, not general intelligence or all middle-school learners.
criteria.implementation: See tools/quality.py and the implementation table in quality-specification.md; semantic judgments remain reviewed records.

criteria.name: Theory, noncoding, coding and assessment linkage
criteria.definition: An objective is aligned when explanation, a prediction or hand-work activity, code application and assessment address the same conceptual relation.
criteria.measurement: Bind activity IDs, locators and concept IDs; require prediction before observation, output interpretation, and an assessment matching the intended performance.
criteria.pass: All required links exist, have matching concept IDs, and substantive review confirms they test the same relation.
criteria.fail: An axis explanation is paired only with unrelated plotting, or an implementation objective is assessed only by terminology recognition.
criteria.uncertainty: Missing artifact or semantic review is uncertain; matching IDs alone does not prove alignment.

examples.normal: Predict axis=0 output length, calculate it, execute the reduction, then explain the agreement.
examples.fault_or_boundary: Running code with the answer visible is guided performance, not independent transfer.

criteria.expected_effect: Expose disconnected activities and unjustified depth claims.
criteria.limits: The link structure is a local operationalization; effectiveness needs learner evidence.
criteria.implementation: See tools/quality.py and the implementation table in quality-specification.md; semantic judgments remain reviewed records.

criteria.name: Theoretical correctness and permissible simplification
criteria.definition: A claim must preserve its quantity, assumptions, domain, mechanism and inferential limits; simplification must not reverse a prediction or decision.
criteria.object: Definitions, explanations, formulas, examples and answer keys
criteria.measurement: Atomize claims; name assumptions and units; compare a primary source or independent derivation; seek a counterexample. Classify false statement, dimensional error, invalid generalization, missing prerequisite step, ambiguity or source conflict.
criteria.pass: Current independent evidence supports the exact scoped claim, including exceptions needed for the intended task.
criteria.fail: A reproducible counterexample or derivation contradicts a material claim or key.
criteria.uncertainty: A source disagreement or unsupported assertion stays uncertain and triggers research; it is not automatically an error.

examples.normal: Precision divides TP by predicted positives, not actual positives.
examples.fault_or_boundary: Validation-based model selection is permitted; fitting preprocessing on validation data is a different operation.

criteria.expected_effect: Prevent teaching a false rule or wrong answer.
criteria.limits: An oracle covers only its declared mathematical case; arbitrary prose still needs expert review.
criteria.implementation: See tools/quality.py and the implementation table in quality-specification.md; semantic judgments remain reviewed records.

criteria.name: Independent numerical and structural checks
criteria.definition: A worked result is independently recomputed from declared inputs and conventions.
criteria.object: Axis reductions, binary metrics, weighted sums and split/fit records
criteria.measurement: Use fixed reference functions, explicit zero-denominator handling, exact fractions where possible and declared tolerances. Test a neighboring valid case as well as an injected fault.
criteria.pass: Reported and independently computed results agree under the same conventions.
criteria.fail: Wrong axis/shape, denominator, value, overlapping split ID or preprocessing fit contamination.
criteria.uncertainty: Undefined ratios without an explicit convention are uncertain, never silently zero.

examples.normal: TP=5 FP=10 FN=5 gives precision 1/3 and recall 1/2.
examples.fault_or_boundary: TP=FP=0 needs a declared undefined-value policy.

criteria.expected_effect: Catch concrete errors without relying on a second self-score.
criteria.limits: Passing these checks does not prove a whole lesson correct or a whole pipeline leakage-free.
criteria.implementation: See tools/quality.py and the implementation table in quality-specification.md; semantic judgments remain reviewed records.

criteria.name: Executable and reproducible material
criteria.definition: A coding claim needs execution of the exact artifact in a recorded environment with meaningful checks.
criteria.measurement: Bind artifact/data digests, command, environment, exit code and result checks; rerun from a clean state and test new input and at least the stated edge cases.
criteria.pass: Current receipts show successful execution and required assertions under the intended environment.
criteria.fail: Nonzero exit, failed assertion, missing input, hidden-state dependence or reported output inconsistent with the receipt.
criteria.uncertainty: No current execution receipt is not_run; a screenshot or copied log alone does not establish execution.

examples.normal: An empty CSV or renamed required column must get its specified outcome.
examples.fault_or_boundary: A successful earlier notebook revision does not validate an edited revision.

criteria.limits: The harness checks receipt bindings, not remote execution authenticity or all possible inputs.
criteria.implementation: See tools/quality.py and the implementation table in quality-specification.md; semantic judgments remain reviewed records.

criteria.name: Assessment meaning and help conditions
criteria.definition: An assessment establishes only the behavior and assistance conditions actually observed.
criteria.measurement: Specify action, input, expected result, scoring rationale, help/answer visibility and a new input where transfer is claimed; independently check keys.
criteria.pass: Assessment demand matches the objective and the reported independence/transfer claim.
criteria.fail: Copied solutions are reported as independent, or a key contradicts an independent calculation.
criteria.uncertainty: Missing observations leave mastery untested; a correct artifact is not learner success.

examples.normal: An unseen confusion matrix with an explanation can assess denominator understanding.
examples.fault_or_boundary: A timed task with hints is not equivalent to an unaided contest task.

criteria.expected_effect: Prevent inflated learning and independence claims.
criteria.limits: Task scores do not establish stable mastery or official exam equivalence.
criteria.implementation: See tools/quality.py and the implementation table in quality-specification.md; semantic judgments remain reviewed records.

criteria.name: Claim-specific direct source support
criteria.definition: A citation supports a claim only when the relevant original content has been read at an adequate extent and scoped correctly.
criteria.object: Each consequential claim and its cited sources
criteria.measurement: Record discovery route, original URL/version, access time, precise location, read extent, finding, limitation and relation to the claim. Empirical effect claims require methods/results/limits, not a search snippet.
criteria.pass: The relevant primary material was read and its scope supports the claim; contradictory evidence is addressed.
criteria.fail: A source is misrepresented, or a search result/abstract is reported as a full-methods review.
criteria.uncertainty: Inaccessible or partially read sources remain uncertain for claims needing the missing sections.

examples.normal: An abstract can support what its abstract says, not an unexamined sample size.
examples.fault_or_boundary: A secondary summary is a discovery lead, not a substitute for the original experiment.

criteria.expected_effect: Make evidence errors and incomplete reading visible.
criteria.limits: Recorded reading is an accountable declaration; the tool cannot authenticate comprehension.
criteria.implementation: See tools/quality.py and the implementation table in quality-specification.md; semantic judgments remain reviewed records.

criteria.name: Research refresh and refinement
criteria.definition: Research repeats when a relevant question, source version, contradiction or failed check changes, and may conclude unchanged or unresolved.
criteria.measurement: Log trigger, focused queries, discovered originals, direct reads, extracted claims, counterevidence, changed/unchanged disposition, and affected IDs. Recheck official sources before production and after relevant notices.
criteria.pass: The current trigger is resolved by scoped evidence or explicitly remains unresolved; unchanged sources preserve applicable results.
criteria.fail: A changed relevant source is ignored, or an unchanged search is described as a verified substantive improvement.
criteria.uncertainty: No result or inaccessible source produces an abstention and a next query, not a fabricated conclusion.

examples.normal: An updated syllabus triggers affected scope/objective reviews.
examples.fault_or_boundary: A spelling change outside a claim does not force every unit to be rewritten.

criteria.expected_effect: Focus repeated investigation on actual uncertainty and change.
criteria.limits: No paper establishes that a fixed 30-minute search schedule is optimal.
criteria.implementation: See tools/quality.py and the implementation table in quality-specification.md; semantic judgments remain reviewed records.

criteria.name: Change impact and current review
criteria.definition: A review is reusable only while its artifact, criterion, source and declared dependency versions match.
criteria.measurement: Traverse reverse dependencies from changed IDs; recompute dependency fingerprints; mark affected reviews stale and keep unrelated valid reviews.
criteria.pass: Every required review is current for its object and dependency closure.
criteria.fail: A changed answer key/source retains an old pass, or known affected work is omitted.
criteria.uncertainty: Unrecorded dependencies remain a documented completeness risk; uncertainty is not a current pass.

examples.normal: Changing the precision definition affects its example, code assertion and assessment key.
examples.fault_or_boundary: Updating an audio-only source should not invalidate an unrelated CSV review.

criteria.expected_effect: Avoid both stale approvals and unnecessary global rework.
criteria.limits: Graph traversal is complete only for the declared edges.
criteria.implementation: See tools/quality.py and the implementation table in quality-specification.md; semantic judgments remain reviewed records.

criteria.name: Duplicate and rejected-work handling
criteria.definition: An unchanged proposal under the same object, criterion, hypothesis and dependency versions is the same attempt; semantic similarity alone is insufficient.
criteria.measurement: Canonicalize exact structured keys; retain accepted, rejected and no-change receipts. Reopen only for a changed dependency, new counterevidence or a different explicit hypothesis.
criteria.pass: Exact duplicates are skipped with their earlier reason; distinct quantities, units and hypotheses remain separate.
criteria.fail: A retired failed proposal is repeated without a new basis, or different meanings are merged because their wording resembles.
criteria.uncertainty: Paraphrases are review candidates, not automatic merges.

examples.normal: Precision and recall share counts but have different denominators and must remain separate.
examples.fault_or_boundary: A new source version permits a new attempt while the old receipt is preserved.

criteria.expected_effect: Reduce repeated work and accidental loss of distinctions.
criteria.limits: The current mechanism does not solve semantic deduplication.
criteria.implementation: See tools/quality.py and the implementation table in quality-specification.md; semantic judgments remain reviewed records.

criteria.name: Severity, priority and bounded completion
criteria.definition: Repair order follows the consequence and certainty of a defect; completion requires the agreed current evidence, not a high average score.
criteria.measurement: Use proposed P0 confirmed false claims/keys or invalid evaluation; P1 required scope, missing prerequisite, missing execution or unresolved blocking evidence; P2 alignment/support improvements; P3 presentation. Within a tier prefer dependency blockers, then broader declared impact, then stable ID. Record checkpoint and finite stop limits.
criteria.pass: A selected action addresses the first eligible nonduplicate blocker; completion has every required current check and no unresolved blocking finding.
criteria.fail: Style is chosen ahead of a confirmed wrong key without a documented dependency reason, or a goal boolean overrides missing evidence.
criteria.uncertainty: Priority policy, thresholds and budgets requiring user choice remain proposed/unset; no automatic execution starts.

examples.normal: Fix a wrong denominator before improving typography.
examples.fault_or_boundary: At 30 minutes report work, evidence, failures, remaining budget and next action; no useful change is valid.

criteria.expected_effect: Make work selection and stopping auditable.
criteria.limits: Priority ordering is a local proposed policy, not an experimentally proven optimum.
criteria.implementation: See tools/quality.py and the implementation table in quality-specification.md; semantic judgments remain reviewed records.

criteria.name: Evaluator calibration and outcome claims
criteria.definition: A reviewer is calibrated only against independently established correct/error cases; educational benefit needs learner evidence.
criteria.measurement: Separate author and reviewer; test known-good and seeded-error controls, reverse order, retain disagreements and untouched cases; distinguish tool tests, content review, suitability and learner outcomes.
criteria.pass: The strength of the conclusion matches actually collected evidence and current independent review.
criteria.fail: Tool tests or a model preference win are presented as learning improvement, or evaluator changes are tested only on their training cases.
criteria.uncertainty: Absent educator calibration or learner data remains untested; tolerances/sample sizes require agreement.

examples.normal: A seeded denominator error tests detection; it is not a student experiment.
examples.fault_or_boundary: No learner study means no claim that students learned more.

criteria.expected_effect: Reduce false confidence in automated judgment.
criteria.limits: Reviewer identity/model-family differences do not ensure independent errors.
criteria.implementation: See tools/quality.py and the implementation table in quality-specification.md; semantic judgments remain reviewed records.
